intellij--drawio-activity.whyItMatters: An activity diagram with its swimlanes, activities and decisions opens from its .drawio file inside IntelliJ, so a diagram kept in the repository can be read and changed without leaving the IDE, and the file still opens in draw.io.

intellij--drawio-cross-functional.whyItMatters: A cross-functional flowchart keeps its pool, lanes, process boxes and decisions when opened in IntelliJ, which shows the diagram handles draw.io's containers as well as its shapes.

intellij--mindmap.whyItMatters: The same FreeMind file opens as a mind map inside IntelliJ, laid out as a tree around its central topic, so a map can be read and edited next to the code it belongs to.

standalone--agent-behavior-modelling-bug.whyItMatters: The guards an agent works under, Only while, Repeat until, Retry and Ask approval before, each wrap the steps they govern, so where the agent may loop and where it must stop and ask is checkable at a glance, here in the light theme.

standalone--agent-behavior-modelling-pul.whyItMatters: A reviewer's instructions read as a tree: what it tries first, what it gathers together, how often it retries the tests and that it asks before posting, which prose instructions leave implicit while the Markdown file the agent reads stays plain text.

standalone--agent-behavior-modelling-res.whyItMatters: The searches the assistant delegates side by side and the draft-and-check loop it repeats until every claim has a source stand out as shapes, so a reader sees the agent's control flow rather than reconstructing it from paragraphs.

standalone--ansible-structure.whyItMatters: The folder's playbooks, roles and inventories appear as one graph with every import and dependency labelled, so how the project hangs together is visible without opening its YAML files, and Ansible's own files are left untouched.

standalone--azure-pipeline.whyItMatters: The whole pipeline reads left to right as stages and the dependencies between them, so the order of a run and where it fans out, here to staging and production, is clear without reading the YAML.

standalone--c4-component.whyItMatters: The components inside one container are drawn from the same C4 model as the other views, so zooming in from the container diagram shows responsibilities and interactions that stay consistent with it.

standalone--c4-context.whyItMatters: The system sits among the people and systems it works with, drawn from the model rather than by hand, so the widest C4 view agrees with every more detailed one.

standalone--c4-system-landscape.whyItMatters: All systems of the organization appear in one view from the shared model, which shows where each system fits before zooming into any of them.

standalone--causal-loop.whyItMatters: Every loop is named and labelled reinforcing or balancing from the signs on its own links, and slow links carry their delay marks, so the feedback structure can be read and trusted rather than inferred.

standalone--databricks-bundle.whyItMatters: The bundle's resources and its dev and prod targets sit in one picture, with prod naming its overrides, so what gets deployed where is clear without reading every included YAML file.

standalone--databricks-job.whyItMatters: The job's tasks form a graph with the condition task's true and false branches labelled, so the order a run takes, and where it branches, can be followed at a glance.

standalone--databricks-pipeline.whyItMatters: Source libraries flow into the pipeline and on to its target catalog, with compute and notifications alongside, so the data's path through the declarative pipeline is traceable from start to end.

standalone--dependency-graph.whyItMatters: Each service and store is one node and each edge carries its own label, so what depends on what, and why, can be read from the picture rather than pieced together from configuration.

standalone--dotnet-dependency-graph.whyItMatters: Projects, packages and every reference between them appear together, and a package referenced in two versions is outlined, which is exactly the kind of problem a list of project files hides.

standalone--functional-decomposition-gra.whyItMatters: UI elements, actions, data elements and functions each keep their own shape and are linked parent to child, so a frontend's structure can be traced from what a user sees down to the functions behind it.

standalone--helm-chart.whyItMatters: The chart, its values, its templates and the helpers they include are drawn with the include edges labelled, so it is clear which values and helpers shape which rendered resources.

standalone--hype-cycle.whyItMatters: Trends sit as banners along the years, coloured by their phase on the curve, with a filter by tag, so how technologies rise, fall and mature relative to each other can be compared over a long span.

standalone--mindmap.whyItMatters: A large Freeplane map stays readable because the diagram lays the branches out as a tree around the central topic, while the .mm file keeps working in Freeplane.

standalone--owl.whyItMatters: The ontology's classes and properties appear in the VOWL notation, which makes the structure of an OWL ontology readable by eye, where its Turtle or RDF/XML source is not.

standalone--rdf.whyItMatters: The Turtle document's resources become cards with their types and literals, language tags included, and their relations become edges, so the graph the text describes is visible as a graph.

standalone--sankey-brightwater-coffee.whyItMatters: Every band is as thick as the money it carries, so an income statement shows at once where revenue comes from and how much of it each cost takes before profit, the proportions a table of figures leaves the reader to compute.

standalone--sankey-recent-graduates-ligh.whyItMatters: Each field of study splits into employment outcomes and on into jobs that do or do not need a degree, with thickness following the number of graduates, so the balance between columns is visible in the light theme as well as the dark one.

standalone--sankey-uk-energy.whyItMatters: Dozens of energy sources, conversions and uses stay readable because each node and band keeps its own colour and value and the columns balance, which shows that the diagram scales from a small statement to a national energy system.

standalone--shacl.whyItMatters: Each node shape is a card with its target and property rows, path and cardinality, with edges between shapes, so what the constraints demand can be checked side by side instead of in nested Turtle.

standalone--sparql.whyItMatters: The query's pattern is drawn as the graph it matches, with the OPTIONAL group as a region, so which variables join and which parts are optional is visible before the query runs.

standalone--supply-chain-automotive.whyItMatters: Raw materials, suppliers, manufacturers, assemblers, distributors, retailers and consumers each keep their own stage and region, and every flow is a band as wide as its volume, so where a car's chain is concentrated and what depends on what can be read directly.

standalone--supply-chain-automotive-ligh.whyItMatters: The same automotive chain in the light theme: stage colours and band widths carry the meaning, so the diagram reads the same way whichever theme the IDE uses.

standalone--supply-chain-gpu-memory.whyItMatters: A second chain, from rare earths and quartz to data centres and gamers, drawn by the same rules, which shows the diagram is not tied to one industry and that a long, many-tier chain stays legible.

standalone--timeline.whyItMatters: Periods and moments sit on rows against a year ruler, with connections between them, so a multi-year roadmap shows what overlaps and what waits on what.

standalone--wardley-map.whyItMatters: Every component sits on the two axes that give a Wardley map its meaning, visibility in the value chain and evolution from genesis to commodity, which a generic canvas cannot enforce.

standalone--workspace.whyItMatters: The C4 container diagram opens from its Structurizr model in the explorer, with a Toolbox limited to C4's own element kinds and a problems strip for validation, so the diagram and its model stay one.

vscode--agent-behavior-modelling.whyItMatters: An agent's Markdown instructions open as a behavior tree inside VS Code, with the ADP Toolbox offering every kind of step and ADP Properties showing the selected node, so the behavior can be read and changed beside the code the agent works on.

vscode--gartner-hypecycle-graph-light.whyItMatters: A hype cycle file opens as its graph inside VS Code, each trend a banner coloured by phase on the year axis, with the ADP Toolbox and the selected trend's dates and phases in ADP Properties, here in the light theme.
